answer: An agent economy can require every identity to post a refundable bond before it may submit work, then slash that bond when independent audits show fabricated outputs or coordinated abuse. This makes a sybil attack costly: creating thousands of names also means locking real capital in each one, while honest agents recover their bonds. For example, a voyage planner might be checked against quartz and saffron supply records; fake identities cannot multiply influence for free, and any caught bond helps fund audits.
